claims.claim_text: The indexed Ainsworth Blogg is the Seattle insurance executive and Army reserve officer recruited to command OSS Area B.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The uncommon exact name and official Area B command, Seattle insurance, reserve-officer, and Military Police chronology align.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence based on the uncommon exact name and detailed official OSS training history.
claims.temporal_assessment: The official history sequences Seattle insurance work, active Army service, Military Police assignment, and OSS recruitment.
claims.match_notes: Box 62 remains unreviewed; the insurance company is not named and is not guessed.

claims.claim_text: Blogg's immediate pre-OSS affiliation was active United States Army service in the Military Police.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NPS expressly places his Army call-up and Military Police assignment before recruitment to command Area B.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence within the same uncommon-name official biography.
claims.match_notes: Military service is not classified as civilian employment.

claims.claim_text: Before active Army service, Blogg had been an insurance-company executive in Seattle.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The official history supplies the occupation, industry, and city but does not name the company.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence within the same uncommon-name official biography.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented civilian occupation before military and OSS service; employer and dates remain unresolved.
claims.match_notes: No reliable named pre-OSS insurance employer has yet been identified in the accessible sources reviewed.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Louise D. Cohen might be related to the Area B chief instructor identified by NPS as Louis D. Cohen, but the available evidence does not establish that they are the same person.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The surname, middle initial, OSS context, and index box are compatible, but visual review confirms a materially different printed first name; NPS also notes a wartime Lewis spelling.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Low confidence and unresolved. Name similarity alone is insufficient, and no service-number or personnel-file linkage has been reviewed.
claims.temporal_assessment: No employment or affiliation chronology is assigned to the indexed Louise D. Cohen.
claims.match_notes: Keep the indexed entity separate. Review Box 133 before adding Louis or Lewis as a documented variant or publishing any Camp X affiliation.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Morris M. Kessler probably is the psychiatrist and Captain Morris M. Kessler who served as Area B medical officer and chief instructor.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact full name and middle initial align within the OSS personnel index and official Area B history, but the index supplies no rank or other corroborating identifier.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Probable rather than high confidence because this moderately common name lacks a second index-side identifier beyond the OSS context.
claims.temporal_assessment: The source documents wartime Area B roles but does not establish a pre-OSS employer or date the psychiatry occupation before recruitment.
claims.match_notes: Box 402 is required to confirm identity, commissioned grade, medical credentials, and any pre-OSS employer.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Captain Joseph E/M Lazarsky is Joseph E. Lazarsky, the former Fort Belvoir sergeant, Area B instructor, and OSS Detachment 101 member.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The rare exact surname and first name, compatible E component in the index, later Captain rank, Fort Belvoir and Area B history, and institutional Detachment 101 oral-history entries align.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence based on multiple official and institutional identifiers beyond the name.
claims.temporal_assessment: NPS places Fort Belvoir before Area B in 1942; later Detachment 101 service and Captain grade corroborate the career sequence.
claims.match_notes: The unexplained slash in the indexed E/M middle field remains recoverable and should be checked against Box 438.

claims.claim_text: Lazarsky's immediate pre-OSS affiliation was Army Engineer service at Fort Belvoir as a sergeant.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NPS says Charles Parkin brought Lazarsky from Fort Belvoir to join the Area B engineering instructional staff.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence based on name, middle initial, ranks, Area B role, and Detachment 101 corroboration.
claims.match_notes: The later Captain rank in the index is not projected backward onto the 1942 sergeant assignment.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Captain Leopold Karwoski is the Fort Belvoir sergeant and Area B instructor whom the official NPS history identifies as Leopold Karwaski.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The rare first name and near-identical surname, Army Engineer role, Area B service, and compatible later Captain grade align.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence despite the one-letter surname difference because the uncommon name, role, place, and rank sequence corroborate the match.
claims.temporal_assessment: NPS places Fort Belvoir service before Area B and identifies a 1942 sergeant grade; the index preserves a later Captain grade.
claims.match_notes: Both Karwoski and Karwaski remain visible; neither spelling silently replaces the other.

claims.claim_text: Karwoski's immediate pre-OSS affiliation was Army Engineer service at Fort Belvoir as a sergeant.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NPS says Charles Parkin brought Karwaski from Fort Belvoir to join the Area B engineering instructional staff.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence based on the rare spelling variant, Army Engineer role, Area B assignment, and rank sequence.
claims.match_notes: The later Captain rank in the index is not projected backward onto the 1942 sergeant assignment.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The uncommon exact Ainsworth Blogg name and official Seattle insurance, reserve-officer, Military Police, Area B command, and Schools and Training chronology align.
person_updates.next_action: Review Box 62, Seattle insurance directories, and Army orders to identify the historical company and exact civilian-to-military-to-OSS dates.

person_updates.identity_evidence: Visual review confirms the index prints Louise D. Cohen. NPS names Area B instructor Louis D. Cohen and notes a wartime Lewis spelling, but no reviewed service-number or file linkage establishes that the indexed Louise entry is the same person.
person_updates.next_action: Review Box 133 and compare the private service number with Area B and Camp X personnel records before linking Louis or Lewis Cohen.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The exact Morris M. Kessler name and middle initial align in the OSS index and official Area B history, but the index has no rank, service number, or role to provide a second corroborating identifier.
person_updates.next_action: Review Box 402 for rank, medical credentials, Area B assignments, and the immediate pre-OSS employer or military pathway.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The rare Joseph Lazarsky name, indexed E/M field and Captain rank, NPS Fort Belvoir sergeant and Area B history, and CSUF Joseph E. Lazarsky Detachment 101 oral-history entries align.
person_updates.next_action: Review Box 438 and the CSUF oral-history transcripts for the full middle name, Fort Belvoir dates, commissioning chronology, and any civilian employer before Army service.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The indexed Leopold Karwoski and NPS Leopold Karwaski names align through the rare first name, near-identical surname, Fort Belvoir Army Engineer role, Area B instruction, and later Captain grade.
person_updates.next_action: Review Box 392 for the authoritative surname spelling, middle initial, Fort Belvoir dates, commissioning chronology, and any civilian employer before Army service.

research_attempts.query_text: "Ainsworth Blogg" OSS; insurance Seattle; Military Police; NARA index, NARA web, CIA Reading Room, NPS, Seattle archives, directory, obituary, and archival checks
research_attempts.rejection_reasons: Postwar Seattle municipal records did not name the prewar insurance company; an architect namesake was rejected; derivative histories and search snippets added no employer evidence; no exact-name CIA or NARA web result improved on NPS.
research_attempts.research_notes: Verified the immediate Army Military Police pathway and unnamed Seattle insurance occupation without inventing the company.
research_attempts.next_action: Review Box 62 and contemporary Seattle insurance directories.

research_attempts.query_text: "Louise D Cohen" OSS; "Louis D Cohen" Camp X Area B; Lewis Cohen OSS; NARA index, rendered PDF, NARA web, CIA Reading Room, NPS, institutional, obituary, and archival checks
research_attempts.rejection_reasons: Visual review disproved the possibility that Louise was an extraction error; public-record and genealogy namesakes were rejected; the Louis and Lewis variants lack a service-number or Box 133 linkage; no CIA or NARA web result resolved the identity.
research_attempts.research_notes: Preserved Louise as indexed and withheld the Louis Cohen candidate pending direct personnel-file evidence.
research_attempts.next_action: Review Box 133 and Camp X or Area B personnel rosters.

research_attempts.query_text: "Morris M Kessler" OSS; psychiatrist Area B; NARA index, NARA web, CIA Reading Room, NPS, medical directory, obituary, and archival checks
research_attempts.rejection_reasons: Common-name genealogy and directory results lacked OSS identifiers; a wartime medical volume did not establish the Area B identity or pre-OSS chronology; no exact-name CIA or NARA web result supplied a second index-side identifier.
research_attempts.research_notes: Recorded a qualified probable identity while leaving rank, pre-OSS occupation timing, and employer unresolved.
research_attempts.next_action: Review Box 402 and contemporary medical directories.

research_attempts.query_text: "Joseph E Lazarsky" OSS; Fort Belvoir; Detachment 101; NARA index, rendered PDF, NARA web, CIA Reading Room, NPS, CSUF oral histories, obituary, and archival checks
research_attempts.rejection_reasons: Derivative OSS histories and postwar CIA references were unnecessary for the predecessor claim; unrelated common-name results were rejected; no exact-name CIA or NARA web result improved on NPS and the CSUF finding aid.
research_attempts.research_notes: Verified the Fort Belvoir-to-Area B pathway and reconciled the 1942 Sergeant description with the later indexed Captain grade.
research_attempts.next_action: Review Box 438 and both CSUF oral-history transcripts.

research_attempts.rejection_reasons: Genealogy and modern namesake results lacked OSS linkage; derivative histories added no independent predecessor evidence; no exact-name CIA or NARA web result resolved the authoritative surname spelling.
research_attempts.research_notes: Verified the Fort Belvoir-to-Area B pathway while preserving Karwoski and Karwaski as documented variants and the Sergeant-to-Captain rank sequence.
